---
title: "Exercise · Cross-Mesh Communication"
---

A short, guided task. Complete it before moving on to the lab.

## Task

For two Picos, one in each of your own meshes, write the subscription
configuration that establishes a relationship using the recipient's
did:webvh:

```yaml
# subscription-a-b.yaml
subscription:
  initiator: did:webvh:https://engine-a.example.com/picos/alice
  recipient: did:webvh:https://engine-b.example.com/picos/bob
  peer:
    initiator: did:peer:rel-alice-bob
    recipient: did:peer:rel-bob-alice
```

Then write a DIDComm message envelope that would be sent after the
subscription is established:

```yaml
# didcomm-message.yaml
message:
  from: did:peer:rel-alice-bob
  to: did:peer:rel-bob-alice
  type: pico/event
  body:
    event: temperature-reading
    value: 21.5
```

::: {.callout-note}
The exact field names are illustrative. The goal is to internalize the flow
from the [lesson](index.qmd): resolve → introduce → create peer DIDs →
establish subscription → encrypted relationship.
:::

## Success criteria

- [ ] Your subscription initiates using the recipient's did:webvh.
- [ ] Your subscription creates a distinct did:peer on each side.
- [ ] Your DIDComm envelope addresses the message by peer DID, not by
      did:webvh.

## Automatable check

Validate both snippets parse:

```bash
pico parse subscription-a-b.yaml --out /tmp/sub.json \
  && echo "OK: subscription parses"
pico parse didcomm-message.yaml --out /tmp/msg.json \
  && echo "OK: message envelope parses"
```

Both commands exit `0` and print the `OK:` line when well-formed.

## Reflect

- Why does the message envelope use did:peer rather than did:webvh after the
  relationship is established?
- What would change if Pico A and Pico B were in the *same* mesh?
